ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Roald Amundsen Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: New patient visit for cold-induced burning pain and numbness in the fingers of both hands: history, examination, blood tests for other causes of neuropathy, mood screening, cold protection, and a neurology referral. Concerns: The pain and clumsiness in his fingers in the cold make him fear he can no longer work in the Arctic; He does not want any medicine that makes him drowsy, because he drives and flies. [S]

tr.td: Diclofenac 1% gel, 4 g to the right ankle four times a day for up to two weeks
four times a day for up to two weeks
Capsaicin 0.075% cream, a small amount rubbed into the painful fingers four times a day; wash hands after use and keep away from the eyes
Duloxetine 30 mg delayed-release capsule, one capsule by mouth daily for one week
Duloxetine 60 mg delayed-release capsule, one capsule by mouth daily; do not stop suddenly

text.paragraph: Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

tr.td: Near-sightedness since youth, partly improved, never fully corrected
Frostbite of the fingers of both hands on a winter ski crossing in his early twenties
Scurvy during thirteen months in the Antarctic pack ice in his mid-twenties, with recovery on fresh seal and penguin meat

Complicated fracture of the right upper arm in a fall on board ship in his mid-forties, set without surgery, with months of self-directed rehabilitation; minor back wounds from a polar bear the same autumn

Near-collapse with palpitations from lamp fumes in a closed observatory, with months of exertional palpitations and a slow recovery; later advised by a heart specialist to give up expeditions, without lasting effect on his exercise tolerance by his account

list.item: Burning pain, numbness and tingling in the fingers of both hands, brought on by cold for many winters and worse this winter, with the fingers turning white then blue then red in the cold; average pain 6 of 10; cause not yet established at intake; nerve conduction studies and neurology consultation requested: resolved, confirmed [S]

Cold-induced neuropathic pain and cold sensitivity of the fingers of both hands, a late sequela of frostbite in early adulthood: small-fiber pattern with normal nerve conduction studies, cold allodynia and reduced pinprick at the fingertips, and cold-induced vasospasm: active, confirmed [S]

Old fracture of the upper end of the right humerus, set at sea and rehabilitated without surgery: forward flexion and abduction limited to about 120 degrees, without pain at rest: active, confirmed [S]

Acute inversion sprain of the right ankle on wet rocks at the shore, lateral ligaments, without fracture by the Ottawa ankle rules; on duloxetine, so no tramadol and a topical rather than an oral NSAID; resolved: resolved, confirmed [S]

tr.td: New patient visit for cold-induced burning pain and numbness in the fingers of both hands: history, examination, blood tests for other causes of neuropathy, mood screening, cold protection, and a neurology referral
Two-week follow-up and neurology consultation with nerve conduction studies
Six-week review: finger pain on capsaicin cream, starting duloxetine
Twelve-week review: finger pain, mood, blood pressure and sodium on duloxetine
Seventeen-week review: finger pain, the ankle sprain, and the risks of an Arctic air search flight
Same-day sick visit for a right ankle sprain

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Neurology consultation in two weeks with nerve conduction studies to confirm or exclude a late post-frostbite neuropathy, entrapment, or another polyneuropathy, and to advise on treatment that does not cause drowsiness

Cold protection and hand care: liner gloves under mittens, heated gloves and hand warmers outdoors, warming the hands before fine work, no cold-water hand washing, and checking the fingers for skin damage
Blood tests for other causes of neuropathy: glucose and HbA1c, vitamin B12, TSH, kidney function, liver enzyme and hemoglobin; PHQ-9 for mood with chronic pain
Capsaicin 0.075% cream to the painful fingers four times a day for localized neuropathic pain, because he wishes to avoid oral treatment, with review in four weeks

Duloxetine 30 mg daily for a week, then 60 mg daily, for neuropathic pain not controlled by capsaicin cream, with review of pain, adverse effects, sleep, mood and blood pressure, a sodium check, no tramadol, and no abrupt stopping
Average finger pain at or below 3 of 10, with fewer cold attacks, by four months
Average pain 2 of 10 on duloxetine 60 mg; cold attacks shorter and less frequent
Able to handle buttons, keys and a pen outdoors in the cold with protective gloves
Managing with liner and heated gloves and hand warmers
Any medicine used causes no daytime drowsiness that affects driving or flying
No drowsiness on capsaicin cream or duloxetine
